clue.text: Had maiden caught in cold shower some offensive words?

indicators.note: the first pieces are held inside the shower word, as if trapped by it

parts.note: hail is a shower of cold ice pellets
had, in the sense of had a meal, means ate
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman, out in a freezing downpour, mutters a few rude words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' means ATE (had dinner); a maiden over in cricket, one with no runs scored, is M on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive letters or messages sent to someone are made up of offensive words.

clue.text: Prime minister on television, one seeking to steal information

definitions.meaning: The fictional premier in the BBC sitcom Yes, Prime Minister
someone who breaks into computer systems to take data

explanation.surface: A TV premier is caught trying to steal data.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes, Prime Minister was a 1980s British TV comedy whose bumbling premier was Jim Hacker.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Hacker was a fictional premier on British TV, and a computer intruder is also called by this name.

clue.text: Emperor's function to keep rule in India

indicators.note: the function word holds the rule word inside it

parts.note: tan, short for tangent, is a trigonometric function
the Raj was British rule in India

explanation.surface: An emperor's job is to maintain rule in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor of the early second century AD.

clue.text: Sugar upset tot before Virginia tucked into fish and duck

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to tot up is to sum, so a tot is a sum

indicators.note: the state abbreviation is placed inside the fish word

parts.note: a cod is a fish
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Spilt sugar, a toddler, and a dish of fish and duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SUM into MUS; a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscovado is an unrefined brown sugar.

clue.text: Put away in vehicle, packed in box: drug smuggled in

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the drug letter is slipped secretly inside the packed word

parts.note: crated means packed in a crate, a box
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs hidden in a crate in a car get someone locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Put away is an idiom for imprisoned, as is incarcerated.

clue.text: Plan to get English degree after school

indicators.note: the English degree is placed following the school abbreviation

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A student's plan: get an English degree once school is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic plan of something.

clue.text: Black stuff with core of soft or hard material

indicators.note: the soft letter forms the middle of the coal word

parts.note: coal is black stuff
P, for piano, means soft in music

explanation.surface: Something black with a soft core, or else a hard material.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) is the musical marking for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes.

clue.text: Them old books? I study something on the computer!

parts.note: 'em is a colloquial shortening of them
OT, the Old Testament, is the old books of the Bible
to con is to study

explanation.surface: Someone scorns old books: 'I study things on a computer!'
explanation.definitionFit: An emoticon is a small typed face or symbol used in online messages.

clue.text: A bit like part of Birmingham, creating surprise?

parts.note: Aston is a district of Birmingham, home of Aston Villa football club
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: Something rather like a corner of Birmingham turns out to be surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston is an area of Birmingham, England's second city; the answer read as ASTON-ISH means a bit like Aston.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze them greatly.

clue.text: Form 1 starts to consider some well-known books

parts.note: a form is a school class
the numeral one is the Roman I

indicators.note: the beginnings of the next two words are taken, as the clue says starts

explanation.surface: A school class is told to look at some famous books.
explanation.definitionFit: Classics are standard, long-admired works of literature that everyone has heard of.

clue.text: After work, seller is to escape getting involved

indicators.note: the seller word is placed following the work word

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
a tout is someone who sells tickets aggressively

explanation.surface: Once the job is done, a salesman just wants to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part, avoiding involvement.

clue.text: Treat bionics unconventionally as medical specialist

indicators.note: treated unconventionally, the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A specialist doctor uses bionic body parts in unusual ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TREAT BIONICS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstetrician is a doctor specialising in pregnancy and childbirth.

clue.text: Source of inspiration in lecture, having switched sides

indicators.note: the letters at the two sides of the word, left end and right end, change places

parts.note: to lecture is to orate

explanation.surface: A talk somewhere manages to inspire, but only after a swap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having switched sides' swaps the first and last letters of ORATE, the O and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry, and the Muses are classical sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Bishop in staggering movement, hero in act of defiance

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is placed within the staggering word

parts.note: to reel is to stagger, so a reel is a staggering movement
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a lion is a brave person, a hero

explanation.surface: A bishop lurches about while a brave figure stands up to authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion is open resistance to authority, a defiant act.

clue.text: Book to excite man into tales

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A book meant to thrill a man by drawing him into its stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MAN INTO TALES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentations is a book of the Old Testament, mourning the fall of Jerusalem.

clue.text: Note penned by investigators for geological study

indicators.note: the note word is shut inside the investigators word

parts.note: tecs is slang for detectives
the tonic is the keynote of a scale

explanation.surface: Detectives write down a note during their investigation of the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tectonics is the study of the earth's crust and the movement of its plates.

clue.text: Weapon housed in rotten stable

indicators.note: the weapon word is lodged inside the rotten word

parts.note: bad means rotten
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: A knight's weapon is kept in a filthy stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a noun for horses but is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something balanced is steady and stable, not likely to tip over.

clue.text: Distress of nurse once, characteristic concealed

indicators.note: the characteristic word is hidden away inside the nurse letters

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, is a former British nursing grade
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: An old-time nurse's distress was a trait she kept hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing grade, since abolished.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to put into difficulty or hardship, to distress.

clue.text: Scot and Austrian working together in a branch of science

indicators.note: the two nationalities' letters are worked over and combined into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scotsman and an Austrian collaborate on some scientific field.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SCOT and AUSTRIAN are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronautics is the science of space travel and spacecraft design.

clue.text: Country with rupee coin

parts.note: a state is a country
R is an abbreviation for rupee

explanation.surface: A nation and its rupee coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was an ancient Greek coin of gold or silver.

clue.text: Carriage provided when Dane, maybe, is given honour

parts.note: Hans is a typical Danish name, as in Hans Christian Andersen
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A carriage is laid on when a Danish man receives an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab.

clue.text: Added time had arisen after injury

indicators.note: after being injured these letters are left disordered, rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer's injury means extra minutes are tacked onto the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Added time' suggests football stoppage time, but the answer is Adar Sheni, the second Adar.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar Sheni is the extra month inserted in Jewish leap years to keep the lunar calendar in step with the seasons.

clue.text: Criticise bargain with Europe, finally

parts.note: a snip is a bargain

indicators.note: the final letter of the Europe word is taken

explanation.surface: A politician attacks a trade deal with Europe at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to make sly critical attacks on someone.

clue.text: Island thus seen looking west from Roman harbour

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
so means thus

explanation.surface: From the old Roman port, one gazes westward toward an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient port of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: Interrupts with instruction to reduce wickedness

parts.note: cut, as an order, tells someone to reduce something
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone butts in with a sermon on cutting back on sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to interrupt a conversation or speaker.

clue.text: Mars — a visit (ET) to be arranged?

indicators.note: these letters are to be put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Should the extraterrestrial set up a visit to the red planet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet but is a verb meaning spoils; the letters of A VISIT ET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitiate is to spoil or impair, just as to mar something is to damage it.

clue.text: City's place of vice, always hiding its face

parts.note: a den is a haunt of vice, as in a den of iniquity

indicators.note: the front letter of the always word is concealed, removed

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A city's den of sin has always kept its true face hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Denver is the capital city of Colorado.

clue.text: Physicist showing anxiety with short memory

parts.note: angst is anxiety
ROM, short for read-only memory, is computer memory

explanation.surface: A scientist shows signs of worry and forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Angstrom was a Swedish physicist, a pioneer of spectroscopy.
